chunks: It was narrated from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: “My daughter made a bequest for a hajj, and she did not perform hajj.” He said: “Then perform hajj on her behalf, for it is for you and for her.”
I said: “My mother died and did not perform hajj.” He said: “Perform hajj on her behalf, for it is for you and for her.”

key_terms.أَوْصَتْ: She made a bequest or will regarding an act to be carried out after her death.
key_terms.بِحَجَّةٍ: For a hajj to be performed on her behalf.
key_terms.لَكَ وَ لَهَا: Its benefit or reward is for both you and her.

ai.seo_question: Can someone perform hajj on behalf of a deceased parent or child in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that hajj may be performed on behalf of a deceased relative who did not perform it, whether a daughter who made a will for it or a mother who passed away without performing it. The Imam عليه السلام explains that the benefit and reward of such an act extend to both the deceased and the one who performs the hajj on their behalf.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2919 - It was narrated from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "My daughter instructed in her will for a Hajj to be performed, but she did not perform Hajj during her lifetime."
Imam (as) said: "Perform Hajj on her behalf; the reward will be for both you and her."

I said: "My mother passed away and did not perform Hajj."
Imam (as) said: "Perform Hajj on her behalf; the reward will be for both you and her."
